title: Simulate forwardRef Pipe
problemStatement: Implement `simulateForwardRef(Component)` that forwards a provided `ref` object as the second argument to `Component(props, ref)`.
interviewTrap: Regular React function components do not accept a `ref` prop; trying to pass `ref` to a normal component warns with 'Function components cannot be given refs'. `forwardRef` is required.

testCases.name: Passes ref object to wrapped component
testCases.testFn: const Comp = simulateForwardRef((props, ref) => ({ type: 'input', refVal: ref.current })); const ref = { current: 'custom-ref-val' }; return Comp({}, ref).refVal;

testCases.name: Passes props along with ref
testCases.testFn: const Comp = simulateForwardRef((props, ref) => ({ name: props.name })); return Comp({ name: 'username' }, {}).name;

testCases.name: Handles null ref gracefully
testCases.testFn: const Comp = simulateForwardRef((props, ref) => (ref ? 'has-ref' : 'no-ref')); return Comp({}, null);

details.name: Passes ref object to wrapped component

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: Normally, refs point directly to the underlying DOM node (`<input>`). `useImperativeHandle(ref, () => ({ customMethod }))` customizes the ref instance exposed to the parent component, hiding raw DOM methods and exposing only clean, intentional APIs.
stepByStepWalkthrough: 1. Render Phase: Fiber node evaluation and hooks linked-list dispatch for Ref Forwarding Through Higher-Order Components.
2. Reconciliation: Double buffering and fiber diffing mechanics.
3. Commit Phase: Synchronous/passive effect execution and DOM mutation.
detailedExplanation.underlyingEngineInternals: In React Fiber, Ref Forwarding Through Higher-Order Components maintains state across work-in-progress trees and lanes scheduling priority.

complexity.time: O(1) per hook / O(N) fiber traversal

interviewCrossQuestions.question: Why does a custom component NOT accept a 'ref' prop by default in React 16-18?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: In React 16-18, `ref` is treated as a reserved system attribute (like `key`) and is stripped from `props`. Passing `ref` to a standard function component logs a warning: `Function components cannot be given refs`. `React.forwardRef` was required to intercept the ref and forward it as a secondary parameter: `(props, ref) => {}`.

interviewCrossQuestions.question: How did React 19 change forwardRef?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: In React 19, `forwardRef` is DEPRECATED! Function components can now accept `ref` directly as a standard prop: `function MyInput({ ref, ...props })`. React 19 treats `ref` as a normal prop, simplifying component design.
interviewCrossQuestions.whyAsked: Checks if candidate is up to date with modern React 19 breaking changes.

realWorldUseCases.description: Allowing parent forms to attach refs to inner `<input>` elements for auto-focus or library integration.
realWorldUseCases.companies: Radix UI, Material UI, Tailwind UI

howToExplain.opening: forwardRef allows components to expose an internal DOM node or instance to parent components via a ref.
keyPoints: In React 16-18, forwardRef forwards ref as second argument (props, ref).
React 19 deprecates forwardRef in favor of ref as a standard prop.
Enables parents to manage focus, scroll, and measurements.
Essential for building reusable design system component primitives.
howToExplain.closingImpression: forwardRef bridges component boundaries to enable imperative DOM interactions when necessary.
analogies: A mailbox slot: the mail carrier drops the letter through the front door slot (forwardRef) directly into the basket inside.

commonMistakes.why: In React DevTools, forwardRef components appear as 'Anonymous' unless a displayName is set.

followUpDeepDive.question: What is WorkTag 11 in React reconciler source?
followUpDeepDive.answer: WorkTag 11 is `ForwardRef`, which executes `renderWithHooks` with `ref` passed as the second argument.
